decisions.id: D2 task's own bundle left un-keyed
decisions.summary: plan-<feature>-<task> (make decide) is not keyed by tree; the plan labels this narrower than the task line's 'key the plan review bundle by tree'
decisions.why: The block's stated reason, that keying it would change the -T<n> shape the plan hold reads, is a cost argument and does not carry this ruling. The ruling rests on a different premise: leaving the name alone leaves no defect. The purpose of the task and of the GM's 2026-11-25 fix ('a review recording in its own tree') is that no reviewer reads a bundle another tree rewrote, or records in the wrong tree. That bundle's name already carries its task. Its MANIFEST already names its tree (T257), as this very bundle's does: diagram-backlog-t271. Each builder works in a worktree of its own task. The GM approved 'a started-task mark per task' (2026-11-25, the same four fixes) so that one task is not started twice. So two trees can only rebuild one task's own bundle if one task is decided in two trees at once, and that is the case the started mark exists to prevent. The block states 'a task has one builder' without measuring it. It holds as far as the started mark does, and no GM word asks for more. The task line's 'by tree' wording is the session's own, not the GM's. If a second tree is ever found deciding a builder's task (the coordinating clone, for example), that is a defect and would need this reopened.

The GM's 2026-11-19 'real enforcement and not just instructions' has as its antecedent the six improvements and four ideas approved that day, which FR-012 scopes to named refusals. Read plainly, it does not reach this 2026-11-25 trials task, and stretching it to T271 would be completing the GM's thought. For the caller to see, not blocking: goal 1 says 'no builder's scratch file overwrites another's', but the mechanism is an instruction. A builder that ignores it can still overwrite another's file, so the goal is aimed at, not guaranteed.

T274 is a measurement task in that sense (it measures the machine to certify the builder count, a throughput lever), and the block's stated reason, 'it makes nothing faster', is the exact reason the GM ruled out. blocks: ### T275 (T267's census: state paths joined onto `<root>/.git` break or are passed over in a linked worktree; measured 2026-11-27 in the pool tree diagram-backlog-t270)

decisions.summary: The reviews and arbiter crates find their review state through the existing l7r_shared common_git_dir resolver. No second resolver is added and no git process is run.
decisions.why: This is a choice of mechanism for fixing a wrong outcome: in a pool tree, the arbiter bundle reported no rounds, no earlier verdict and no snapshot. It narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: The state is read and written in the clone's common git directory from any tree. A plain clone's paths are unchanged because there the common directory is <root>/.git.
decisions.why: The block says every writer of this state already writes to the clone's directory (the pair guard's state, make verify's --state). So reading per tree is the defect and reading the common directory is its fix. This is not the 2026-11-25 'a review recording in its own tree' fix, which is the plan-verdict record that the MANIFEST says is run from the plan's own tree (451 T257). No block moves that record.

decisions.summary: The fix covers reviews (prereq verdict_dir, disposition_dir, stale_maps snapshots, write_verdict pairing-state, tree::of_unit and gate_file, scoped_dir, the snapshot destination) and arbiter (sections round_counter, reviews review_verdicts, which drops its rev-parse process). Red-first tests run on a real git worktree.
decisions.why: Each item is a site the census found that the arbiter bundle or the reviews crate reaches. The tests fail only when the requested behavior is missing, so they are enforcement and not added scope.

decisions.summary: snapshot/tests.rs faked an unwritable snapshot with a .git file naming a missing directory. It now names a git directory that is a file, so the same error is still raised.
decisions.why: The fixture relied on the bug being fixed. Changing it keeps the test checking the same refusal.

decisions.summary: clone_sync_hooks .join(.git).is_dir() probes stay on purpose: a pool tree must not claim to be the session's clone. archive/store.rs:161 probes $HOME/source-archive, which is always its own clone.
decisions.why: The block gives a reason for each that is correct behavior and not a wrong outcome, so neither is a defect and leaving them needs no ruling.

decisions.summary: The guard's state joined onto the session cwd in a worktree has a visible effect (the finished-run reminder repeats at every Stop in a pool tree). It is not fixed here and is filed as T441, 'lands before T22'.
decisions.why: This leaves a known wrong outcome out of this task, so it is a narrowing. The ground for it is not cost ('guard files, outside this task's crates' legitimizes nothing). The ground is the GM's own rule on known defects: fix them before the next step of the port begins (2026-11-18; 'fix all of this as part of our tasking that we are doing before resuming our port', 2026-11-26). T441 is filed in this same feature, which is that pre-port tasking, so the defect is scheduled and not carried into the port. The item also has the form FR-009 asks for: why it is not fixed here, the filed id and an order. The bundle does not say what T22 is. The ruling rests on T441 being a task of 451 and so landing before the port resumes, whatever T22 turns out to be.

decisions.id: D7 T442 deferral (tree-own git-dir readers and the gate's other .git joins)
decisions.summary: The review-verdict readers that take a tree's own git directory (a checkpoint or tick in a pool tree misses a recorded verdict) and the gate's other .git joins (stale_terms.rs, helpers.rs quote-verbatim, approach-owed) are not fixed here and are filed as T442, 'lands before T22'.
decisions.why: This covers two unlike things, so each is judged on its own. (a) The readers of the tree's own git directory have the same defect as D3, reached through rev-parse rather than a .join. (b) The other .git joins are separate sites. For both, 'more sites than one builder's brief allows' is a cost reason and legitimizes nothing. What makes each legitimate is the same as for D6: they are filed in 451, the GM's pre-port tasking, with FR-009's why, id and order. They are also measured as not reached by builder commands, from the transcripts' count of make targets. A note for T442: the census method this block states searches .git join strings only, and its shell pattern is elided with '...'. It does not name rev-parse --git-dir / --absolute-git-dir or other ways of reaching a tree's own git directory, which is how review_verdicts reached it. T442's own census should search those forms and give its pattern in full. No instance is shown left unfiled, so this does not change the ruling.
